speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if the double vision worsens when you look down or up, or does it remain constant? Also, have you noticed any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of fluctuating weakness and vertical diplopia is very telling. Can you tell me exactly how many steps you can climb before struggling, and do you experience any drooping of your eyelids? Also, do you have a history of myasthenia gravis or Lambert-Eaton syndrome?

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies, Anti-MuSK_antibodies, Repeated_Nerve_Conduction_Studies

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Anti-MuSK_antibodies: Not detected; Repeated_Nerve_Conduction_Studies: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies confirms Myasthenia Gravis. Based on your symptoms and test results, are you currently taking any medications for this condition, or is this your first presentation? Do you experience significant fatigue in your upper eyelids (ptosis) as well as your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. Given the positive acetylcholine receptor antibodies and classic fluctuating weakness with vertical diplopia, your diagnosis is confirmed. I recommend an MRI of the brain to rule out a thymoma, which is associated with this condition. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast.
